newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French Dec consumer spending falls.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French Dec consumer spending falls.

text.p: Following are economists' comments after French national statistics institute INSEE said consumer spending fell 0.8 percent in December after a revised 0.5 percent fall in November.

What we are seeing is the reverse of the good numbers from the summer. There were a number of factors weighing. The weather had an effect and the fact that there were only four Saturdays in the period compared to five in November. Also, the timing of Christmas and New Year encouraged people to take two weeks off.
This shows that the recovery in the short term will be slow. We don't expect to see a robust rebound until the second half of 1997.

I think the market was looking for something stronger but these figures do tend to be volatile. The concern is really about fourth quarter GDP, as I wouldn't expect much market impact -- perhaps the (bond) spreads coming in a little.
There was terrible weather and you do often see a see-saw pattern in durables (goods)
It's quite a bit weaker than I thought.

We were expecting a drop but a smaller drop than the one we saw. It's not surprising. It confirms that consumer spending in the fourth quarter was pretty weak and that consumer spending's contribution to fourth-quarter gross domestic product will be negative.
On the other hand we are expecting a rebound in January, which will be partly due to sales that began on Janaury 3 this year and that plays an important role.
